memoryText: But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, born of woman, born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Galatians 4:4-5 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Four phrases carry the verse.

“When the fullness of time had come.” History is not random. God had been preparing for centuries, through Abraham, Moses, David, and the prophets, until the moment he chose. The coming of Christ was right on schedule.

“God sent forth his Son, born of woman, born under the law.” The Son existed before he was sent. He was born of a woman, fully human, and born under the law, placing himself under the obligations of God’s covenant with Israel. He lived the life we should have lived.

“To redeem those who were under the law.” Redemption means buying back, the price paid to free a slave. He kept the law that we broke and bore the curse that we deserved.

“So that we might receive adoption as sons.” The goal is not just freedom, but family. We are not simply released; we are welcomed home.

Whenever you feel like a stranger or an orphan, say this verse. You were bought at a price in order to be brought home.
weekInReview: This week you began the unit on law, gospel, and the church by reading Galatians, Paul’s urgent defense of the gospel. In Galatians 1 and 2 you saw that there is no other gospel, that Paul’s message came by revelation, and that he opposed Peter at Antioch because the gospel is at stake in how we live together. In a doctrinal pause on adoption, you saw how the Father sent the Son and the Spirit so that sinners could become sons and daughters and cry “Abba! Father!” In Galatians 3 and 4, you read the case from Scripture: Abraham was justified by faith, Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, the law was a temporary guardian, and in Christ all are sons and heirs. You also saw Paul’s allegory of Hagar and Sarah, with the contrast between slavery and freedom.
reflectionQuestions: Paul says the gospel cannot be added to. Is there anything you tend to add to faith in Christ as a requirement for being accepted by God, such as performance, a feeling, or a ritual? How does the cross answer that?
Galatians 3:13 says Christ became a curse for us. How does it affect you to know that Jesus took the curse that belonged to you? What does this make you want to say to him?
Which is harder for you to believe: that you are forgiven, or that you are a beloved son or daughter of the Father? What might help you rest in your adoption this week?
prayerPrompts: Thank God for sending his Son to redeem and adopt you.
Ask him to quiet any fear of not belonging.
